discovery: First laboratory demonstration of fusion ignition and target energy gain in inertial confinement fusion

nominees.name: Alex B. Zylstra
nominees.affiliation: Pacific Fusion (formerly Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory), USA

motivation: After six decades of effort, the National Ignition Facility achieved a burning plasma (2021), then ignition by the Lawson criterion, and on 5 December 2022 produced 3.15 MJ of fusion yield from 2.05 MJ of laser energy, the first controlled fusion reaction with target gain above unity. Later shots reached more than 8 MJ and gain above four. Hurricane led the scientific strategy that established alpha-heating-dominated implosions. Kritcher led the design of the high-yield HYBRID-E capsules. Zylstra led the experiments and analysis that demonstrated the burning-plasma and ignition regimes. This work turns a central question of plasma physics into a measured fact: a self-heating thermonuclear plasma can be created and diagnosed in the laboratory. It demanded first-principles understanding of hydrodynamic instabilities, radiation transport and alpha-particle deposition, tested against precise neutron diagnostics. It is physics that has changed what experimentalists and engineers can build.
